message: Two kids (4 and 7), my husband and I both work full time. Combined take-home is about $7,800/month. Rent $2,400, daycare for the little one $1,350, car payment $420. Every month we somehow end up with nothing left and I can't figure out where it goes. I want to set up an actual budget but there are a million methods. Bit of background: I'm a parent of two, went back to work part-time doing admin at a small dental clinic, and the owner has started asking me to pull numbers from our patient database since I'm 'good with computers'. I've been learning SQL in the evenings for about three weeks. Our system is on MySQL. I wrote this and it gives me way more rows than there are patients:

SELECT p.name, a.appointment_date
FROM patients p
JOIN appointments a ON p.id = a.patient_id;

Why is it returning so many rows?

I tried removing the PK and now I have duplicate sample rows everywhere with slightly different metadata. This is a mess.

My query to get the top 3 most-cited papers per year from my citations table is returning wrong results. Some years have 5 rows, some have 2. Here's what I wrote:

SELECT year, title, citations
FROM papers p
WHERE (
  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM papers p2
  WHERE p2.year = p.year AND p2.citations > p.citations
) < 3
ORDER BY year, citations DESC;

Postgres 15. Can you look at it and tell me what's wrong?

I work from home as a freelance designer and I've been living on toast and takeout for months, so I decided to start meal prepping on Sundays. I'm cooking for just me, budget around 60 euros a week, I have a small kitchen with two burners and an oven, and I don't love eating the exact same thing every day. Here's my first attempt at a plan, can you tell me if it's realistic or where it falls apart?

Sunday prep:
- big pot of chickpea curry (4 portions)
- tray of roasted veg (peppers, courgette, red onion, sweet potato)
- 6 chicken breasts baked with paprika
- pot of quinoa
- 6 hard-boiled eggs

Week:
- lunches: quinoa + roasted veg + chicken, Mon-Fri
- dinners: chickpea curry Mon-Thu, Friday takeout
- breakfast: 2 eggs + toast
- snacks: whatever

I'm guessing it'll take 2 hours on Sunday.
